title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010
why_relevant: Defines architecture descriptions in terms of stakeholders, concerns, viewpoints, views, and correspondences rather than a flat document pile.
claims_supported: Top-level documentation should be organized by concern and role.
Correspondences between documentation artifacts should be explicit.

title: Documenting Software Architectures in an Agile World
publisher: Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
why_relevant: SEI guidance that architecture documentation must be understandable and structured for stakeholder use.
claims_supported: Architecture documentation should be readable and audience-shaped.
Not every document belongs in the same primary reading path.

title: A Practical Method for Documenting Software Architectures
publisher: Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
why_relevant: Views and Beyond-oriented documentation method for selecting and packaging the documentation that stakeholders actually need.
claims_supported: Documentation should be organized as a deliberate set of views.
Top-level architecture communication should be curated.

title: Requirements Tracing
why_relevant: Supports explicit traceability across artifacts instead of informal memory.
claims_supported: A machine-readable registry is justified for documentation traceability.

title: Using AI to Augment Repository READMEs
publisher: Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
why_relevant: Supports generated repository summaries and README augmentation as useful derived artifacts rather than canonical authored truth by default.
claims_supported: Generated summaries can be rebuildable support artifacts.
Generated inventories should be distinguished from canonical authored docs.

title: RepoSummary: Feature-Oriented Repository Summarization
why_relevant: Repository summarization research supporting structured, task-aware summaries over raw flat code/document surfaces.
claims_supported: Large repository surfaces benefit from curated summaries and structured entrypoints.

title: ModARO: Multi-Model Architecture Reconstruction and Analysis Framework
why_relevant: Architecture reconstruction research supporting explicit structure recovery and layered model views.
claims_supported: Architecture-facing repositories benefit from explicit recovered structure rather than flat file lists.

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
why_relevant: Supports lightweight context -> decision -> consequences structure for documentation-governance choices.
claims_supported: Documentation governance decisions should be explicitly recorded with rationale and consequences.
